To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) perceived warmth is a stronger predictor than perceived competence of COO evaluations; (b) the impact of national stereotypes depends on the product type and the consumer characteristics; (c) national stereotypes are a more important determinant of COO evaluations than consumer characteristics; and (d) the interaction between product type and consumer characteristics is stronger than the interaction between product and national stereotype dimensions.
the warmth and competence dimensions of national stereotype contents have an effect on COO evaluations of products.
national stereotypes are a key factor in explaining COO effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of national stereotypes in shaping consumer evaluations of products and the potential interactions with other factors, such as product type and consumer characteristics.
the impact of national stereotypes and the perceived dimensions of warmth and competence on COO based evaluations.
the impact of national stereotypes, as a key component of the COO construct, on consumer evaluations of products from a country of origin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

national stereotype contents, such as the perceived warmth and competence of a nation, have a significant effect on the COO effects of products and that this effect is mediated by product characteristics and consumer characteristics.
national stereotypes have a significant effect on the COO based evaluations of products.
the impact of national stereotypes and COOs on product evaluations is moderated by the product type, consumer characteristics and the interaction effects of these factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
national stereotypes are important in the formation of COO effects and the effects of COO on consumer evaluations of products and services.
the impact of national stereotypes can be decomposed into the perceived competence and perceived warmth of a nation.
the conceptualization of the relationship between national stereotyping dimensions and COO effects is important for both academics and practitioners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
national stereotypes are a useful construct for understanding and predicting consumer evaluations of products from different nations.
national stereotypes can have a significant influence on COO evaluations and this effect can be further moderated by product type.

COO based evaluations can be predicted based on the dimensions of national stereotype contents and that the effects of these contents can be moderated by the type of product and consumer characteristics.
